title: Only 7% Pass This Midwifery Entrance Exam
summary: Explore First Appointment, Pregnancy & Birth, Respect & Safety, Labour & Newborn Decisions, Final Birth Centre across five six-question rounds.

landing.intro:
Read the clues. Make the connections.
Put your thinking to the test.

about.body:
Five rounds offer different angles on this challenge: First Appointment, Pregnancy & Birth, Respect & Safety, Labour & Newborn Decisions, Final Birth Centre. Each round contains six distinct questions.

Choose one of four answers and move on automatically. There is no time limit. A short rewarded ad opens the quiz, each next round and the final result. The target is 24 correct answers out of 30. The result describes this quiz attempt only.

For entertainment and general learning only. This is not an accredited midwifery entrance examination, clinical assessment, professional qualification or medical advice. Maternity-care procedures and responsibilities vary; always follow local policy and qualified clinical guidance.

steps: Press Start, watch a short rewarded ad and begin.
Choose one answer per question and progress through five rounds.
Complete all 30 questions to reveal your result. You can then unlock the full breakdown.

insights.overview: Your midwifery score at a glance

mid-r1q1.question: Which organ supports exchange during pregnancy?

answers.a1: Bladder
answers.a3: Pancreas

mid-r1q2.question: Why are observations recorded at more than one appointment?

answers.a1: To make every value identical
answers.a3: To predict an exact birth time
answers.a4: To notice changes and trends over time

mid-r1q3.question: What does the cervix do during labour?

answers.a1: It gradually opens as labour progresses
answers.a3: It produces milk

mid-r1q4.question: What helps a stable newborn conserve warmth soon after birth?

answers.a1: A cold bath
answers.a3: Drying and skin-to-skin contact

mid-r1q5.question: When should hands be cleaned around maternity care?

answers.a1: Only at the end of a shift
answers.a3: Before clean contact and after exposure risk

mid-r1q6.question: A woman says, “I’m worried about what happens next.” What is the best first response?

answers.a1: Acknowledge the worry and invite her questions
answers.a2: Say there is nothing to worry about
answers.a3: Change the subject

mid-r2q1.question: Where does a baby normally develop during pregnancy?

answers.a1: Inside the bladder
answers.a3: Inside the uterus

mid-r2q3.question: What connects the baby to the placenta?

answers.a1: The cervix
answers.a3: The umbilical cord

visual.ariaLabel: Maternal blood to placenta to cord to baby

mid-r2q4.question: Which sequence best represents oxygen reaching the baby?

answers.a1: Baby → stomach → placenta → lung
answers.a3: Placenta → bladder → cord → baby

mid-r3q2.question: A new severe headache appears with visual changes during pregnancy. What is the safest response?

answers.a1: Rest and reassess after an hour
answers.a2: Wait for the next routine appointment
answers.a3: Ask someone at home to keep an eye on the symptoms
answers.a4: Seek prompt assessment from a qualified maternity professional

mid-r3q4.question: A chart records 70, 74 and 78 at three visits. What does it show?

answers.a1: No change
answers.a3: A missing measurement

mid-r5q4.question: The baby is born but the placenta is not yet delivered. Which labour stage is this?

answers.a1: The third stage
answers.a3: The second stage

mid-r4q4.question: A woman becomes tearful and says she feels overwhelmed. What should happen first?

answers.a1: Move straight into practical advice
answers.a2: Pause, acknowledge how she feels and listen
answers.a3: Reassure her that feeling overwhelmed is common
answers.a4: Try to distract her from what is upsetting her

mid-r5q6.question: Equipment’s sterile wrapper is torn before use. What is the safest response?

answers.a1: Do not treat it as sterile; replace or escalate appropriately
answers.a3: Hide the tear
answers.a4: Touch the contents to test them

mid-r4q1.question: A clean procedure is about to begin. What is essential immediately beforehand?

answers.a1: Touch several shared surfaces
answers.a3: Skip cleaning if hands look clean

mid-r4q2.question: A task may splash body fluid towards the eyes. What is the safest preparation?

answers.a1: Turn the face away only
answers.a2: Wear ordinary glasses as the only protection
answers.a3: Use appropriate eye or face protection

mid-r4q3.question: A woman says she does not want students present. What is the best response?

answers.a1: Tell her attendance removes that choice
answers.a2: Discuss her refusal in the corridor
answers.a3: Respect her decision and protect her privacy

mid-r4q6.question: A woman asks to consider her options before deciding. What is the respectful response?

answers.a1: Pressure her into the quickest option
answers.a3: Treat questions as refusal of care
answers.a4: Give clear information, answer questions and allow appropriate time

items: NOW::Feels feverish · shaking · suddenly much worse
visual.ariaLabel: Earlier comfortable and alert. Now feels feverish, is shaking and suddenly feels much worse.

answers.a1: The time printed on the chart
answers.a2: The fact that labour began earlier
answers.a3: The colour of the blanket
answers.a4: The combined feverish feeling, shaking and marked change from earlier

mid-r7q2.question: Which pattern most strongly suggests a stable newborn may be ready to feed?

answers.a1: Turning towards touch, mouth opening and increasing alertness
answers.a3: Persistent irregular breathing and poor responsiveness
answers.a4: Becoming progressively colder and less active

mid-r7q4.question: What is the basic aim of skin-to-skin contact for a stable newborn?

answers.a1: Cool the baby quickly
answers.a2: Support warmth, calm contact and early feeding
answers.a3: Keep parent and baby apart

mid-r5q2.question: Which visible pattern is most useful when describing contractions?

answers.a1: Their frequency, duration and change over time
answers.a3: The clock colour

mid-r5q3.question: Which change best describes labour becoming more established?

answers.a1: Contractions become generally stronger, longer and more regular
answers.a3: The placenta is always delivered before the baby
answers.a4: The cervix returns to its pre-pregnancy state

mid-r7q3.question: A newborn is not feeding as usual and is breathing noticeably faster. What is safest?

answers.a1: Wait several days without telling anyone
answers.a3: Give an unprescribed treatment
answers.a4: Recognise the change and seek prompt qualified assessment

items: PERSON A::Comfortable · alert · routine feeding question
PERSON B::New heavy bleeding · pale · dizzy
visual.ariaLabel: Person A is comfortable and alert with a routine feeding question. Person B has new heavy bleeding and is pale and dizzy.

answers.a1: Person A, because routine questions are quicker
answers.a2: Both can wait for the next handover
answers.a3: Person B, because sudden bleeding, pallor and dizziness show deterioration

mid-r7q5.question: How should a clean, dry umbilical cord stump generally be treated?

answers.a1: Cover it with unprescribed substances
answers.a2: Keep it clean and dry and seek advice if concerning changes appear
answers.a3: Pull it to make it detach

mid-r9q1.context: 14:00: comfortable, normal colour, speaking normally. 15:00: breathing faster, pale and increasingly difficult to engage.
mid-r9q1.question: Which change in the handover should receive the greatest attention?

answers.a1: The observation was recorded one hour later
answers.a2: Several new signs show deterioration from the earlier baseline
answers.a3: The first record contains fewer words

mid-r10q1.context: The placenta is the exchange organ. A diagram now shows reduced transfer across it and less oxygen in the cord.
mid-r10q1.question: Which explanation best links both observations?

answers.a1: Reduced placental exchange can mean less oxygen reaches the baby
answers.a3: The cervix produces oxygen
answers.a4: The stomach supplies the cord directly

mid-r10q2.context: Fluid chart: 650 mL + 450 mL. Observation chart: earlier 74, latest 82.
mid-r10q2.question: What total and trend should be handed over?

answers.a1: 650 mL total with no change
answers.a2: 1,100 mL total, with the latest observation higher than the first
answers.a3: 1,650 mL total with a falling trend

mid-r10q3.context: Earlier: regular contractions with comfortable pauses. Now: constant severe pain, pallor and faintness.
mid-r10q3.question: What is the safest conclusion?

answers.a1: The regular pattern means every later change is normal
answers.a2: Wait until the next planned check
answers.a3: Choose a named diagnosis before reporting
answers.a4: The sudden multi-clue change needs urgent qualified assessment
